name: io.github.2016judea/artists-in-residence
title: Artists in Residence
description: Real public-domain works by Leonardo, Newton, Cajal, Lissitzky and Hine, with credit and licence

tools.name: list_artists
tools.description:
Lists the artists in residence: who they are, their dates, how many public-domain works each has in the catalog, what kinds of work those are, the tool that searches each one, and example subjects.

Example invocations:
- "Which artists are in Artists in Residence?"
- "What can I search for in the Lewis Hine collection?"
- "How many Leonardo drawings are there?"

tools.name: leonardo_da_vinci
tools.description:
Searches 625 public-domain works by Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519) catalogued from open-access museum and library collections. Drawings and notebook pages: anatomy, machines and flight, water and storms, horses, heads and caricatures, drapery, plants, landscapes, maps. Pen and brown ink, red chalk, metalpoint, tempera on linen, mirror-script notes. Returns the best matches for a subject: the first as an image, and every match with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link. With no subject, returns highlights. Real works only; nothing is generated.

Example invocations:
- "Find Leonardo da Vinci works showing flying machines"
- "Find Leonardo da Vinci works showing horses"
- "Find Leonardo da Vinci works showing the skull"

subject.description: What to look for, in plain words: a subject, motif, place, medium or year (e.g. "flying machines").

limit.description: How many matches to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: isaac_newton
tools.description:
Searches 205 public-domain works by Sir Isaac Newton (1643–1727) catalogued from open-access museum and library collections. Pages and figures from his own books and manuscripts: the Principia (1687 and the editions he oversaw), the Opticks, his notebooks and papers. Engraved geometric figures with lettered points, orbits, prisms and lenses, title pages, handwritten pages. Returns the best matches for a subject: the first as an image, and every match with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link. With no subject, returns highlights. Real works only; nothing is generated.

Example invocations:
- "Find Sir Isaac Newton works showing orbits"
- "Find Sir Isaac Newton works showing the Principia title page"
- "Find Sir Isaac Newton works showing a manuscript page"

subject.description: What to look for, in plain words: a subject, motif, place, medium or year (e.g. "orbits").

limit.description: How many matches to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: ramon_y_cajal
tools.description:
Searches 44 public-domain works by Santiago Ramón y Cajal (1852–1934) catalogued from open-access museum and library collections. His drawings of the nervous system (Golgi-stained neurons, glia, the retina, the cerebellum, sections of the brainstem and spinal cord) in pen and India ink, and photographs he took. Returns the best matches for a subject: the first as an image, and every match with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link. With no subject, returns highlights. Real works only; nothing is generated.

Example invocations:
- "Find Santiago Ramón y Cajal works showing neurons"
- "Find Santiago Ramón y Cajal works showing the retina"
- "Find Santiago Ramón y Cajal works showing glia"

subject.description: What to look for, in plain words: a subject, motif, place, medium or year (e.g. "neurons").

limit.description: How many matches to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: lewis_hine
tools.description:
Searches 6943 public-domain works by Lewis Hine (1874–1940) catalogued from open-access museum and library collections. Documentary photographs: children at work in mills, mines, fields and streets for the National Child Labor Committee (1908–1924), and work portraits and the Empire State Building going up (1920s–30s). Gelatin silver prints. Returns the best matches for a subject: the first as an image, and every match with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link. With no subject, returns highlights. Real works only; nothing is generated.

Example invocations:
- "Find Lewis Hine works showing the Empire State Building"
- "Find Lewis Hine works showing textile mills"
- "Find Lewis Hine works showing newsboys"

subject.description: What to look for, in plain words: a subject, motif, place, medium or year (e.g. "the Empire State Building").

limit.description: How many matches to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: el_lissitzky
tools.description:
Searches 190 public-domain works by El Lissitzky (1890–1941) catalogued from open-access museum and library collections. Works dated 1930 or earlier only (US public domain): Prouns, the 1923 Victory over the Sun figurines, posters, book and magazine design, typography, photomontage. Returns the best matches for a subject: the first as an image, and every match with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link. With no subject, returns highlights. Real works only; nothing is generated.

Example invocations:
- "Find El Lissitzky works showing Prouns"
- "Find El Lissitzky works showing posters"
- "Find El Lissitzky works showing the Victory over the Sun figurines"

subject.description: What to look for, in plain words: a subject, motif, place, medium or year (e.g. "Prouns").

limit.description: How many matches to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: public_domain_art_about
tools.description:
Searches all five artists' catalogs at once (Leonardo da Vinci, Isaac Newton, Santiago Ramón y Cajal, El Lissitzky, Lewis Hine; about 8,000 public-domain works) for one subject, and returns the matches with how many each artist has, each work's credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link, and the first as an image.

Example questions:
- "Find a public-domain image of a horse"
- "Free-to-use historical art of machines"
- "Public-domain pictures of factories"

subject.description: The subject in plain words, e.g. 'horse', 'factory', 'brain'.

limit.description: How many works to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: how_to_credit_artwork
tools.description:
Looks up one work by its title (as shown in a result or typed from memory) and returns its credit line, its licence as the holding institution states it, the institution, the source page, and a ready attribution line.

Example questions:
- "How do I credit the Vitruvian Man?"
- "Can I use Lewis Hine's Icarus, Empire State Building?"
- "What's the licence on Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge?"

artist.description: Optional artist name, to narrow the lookup.

tools.name: art_from_year
tools.description:
Public-domain works across the five artists dated to one year or a span of years (works with no recorded year are left out), with how many each artist has in that span, and each work's credit, licence and source page.

Example questions:
- "Art made in 1910"
- "What was Leonardo drawing around 1505?"
- "Photographs from 1908 to 1912"

limit.description: How many works to list (1-10, default 5).

tools.name: artwork_of_the_day
tools.description:
One highlighted public-domain work for today (UTC), the same for everyone all day, rotating through the five artists' highlights, with its credit, licence, source page and image.

Example questions:
- "Show me today's artwork"
- "Give me a random public-domain artwork"
- "Art of the day"

tools.name: child_labor_photographs
tools.description:
Lewis Hine's National Child Labor Committee photographs (1908–1924): children at work in mills, mines, canneries, fields and on city streets, with his own captions. Real public-domain works from open-access collections, each with title, date, medium, holding institution, credit, licence, source page and full-resolution link; the first comes back as an image.

Example questions:
- "Show me Lewis Hine's child labor photos"
- "Child labor photographs from cotton mills"
- "Historic photos of kids working in coal mines"
